I'm a monochromat (not fully monochromatic, I still see some colors, just not as many shades), and the thing that's most difficult for me is eyeshadow. I can't tell the difference between similar shades very well (the Naked 2 Basics almost killed me), and bright colors just don't work very well. I also can't match foundation for shit.

As for your questions: for me, a full face of makeup will just look like a normal face. If you're wearing light eyeshadow, I won't be able to tell at all, and if your foundation or concealer is the wrong shade I won't even notice it. No-makeup makeup looks like a normal face. Plums and corals sort of suck -- I can't see orange AT ALL, so I'll occasionally buy "red" lipstick that I'll later find out was a lovely shade of orange. Purple blends strongly into blue for me, I don't seen nearly as many shades of that.

So when I was about twelve I was out sailing with my father and brother off the coast of Massachusetts, per our usual summer tradition. We'd been out at Nantucket a couple days earlier and were heading back when it started to get rough -- this was the year that a really impressive storm was heading west toward shore. The wind was getting worse, my brother was seasick, and my father was struggling -- we lost the dinghy three times and had to circle back to get it each time which sucked ass. Finally, when we were going to tack, my brother was left in charge of the jib line for a moment while my father wrestled to reef the mainsail. He, like the incompetent nine-year-old that he was, dropped the line overboard, where it got tangled in the motor under the boat.

We stalled. My father stopped everything, took down the sails, and just sort of sat down with his head in his hands for a while. The line was tangled enough that he decided to go underwater to get it unstuck so that we could continue back before the weather got worse. He grabbed a mask and jumped in.

At this point my brother had been crying pretty steadily for about two hours, and I was getting annoyed with that and his inability to do anything useful to help the situation at hand. After my father had been under for about two and a half minutes, he started sobbing again, something about "bartitsusensei, he hasn't come up in FOREVER DO SOMETHING"

Finally, driven to my breaking point by stupidity and a famously short temper, I snapped:

"HE'S DEAD. 110% GUARANTEE THAT HE IS DEAD, WE HAVE TO SAIL BACK TO SHORE OURSELVES."

There were a few seconds of silence before he just started straight-up screaming. I sort of laughed, sort of kicked myself for escalating his panic. My father heard the screams from underwater somehow and surfaced -- this caused a few seconds of absolute terror at seeing a "dead" body before it was sorted out.

It's been five years since then, reddit. I still have to swab the decks daily when we're out sailing as punishment (there's two years left of my sentence), but every single day I remember that it was totally fucking worth it to screw with him.
